lines.text: Queen Mary copied her grandmother's tiara.
Her grandmother owned a tiara of diamond lover's knots.
It went to Mary's aunt, so Mary could not inherit it.
In 1913, she asked the court jeweler Garrard to make a copy.

post.caption: Queen Mary copied her grandmother's tiara. Her grandmother, the Duchess of Cambridge, owned a tiara of diamond lover's knots, but it went to Mary's aunt, so Mary could not inherit it. In 1913 she asked the court jeweler Garrard to make a copy, using diamonds and pearls from her own collection. Nineteen pearls hang from the knots, and pearls once stood upright on top, taken from another tiara. Queen Elizabeth the Second inherited it in 1953, Princess Diana began wearing it in 1981, and Catherine first wore it in 2015 at a diplomatic reception.
